item.title: Good, but a few things here
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, Euclid, not Keter. It can be locked in a box and probably nothing bad would happen. Don’t see why Keter.

Also, ending is too abrupt. This doesn’t seem like a finished file. Just add a few sentences to wrap things up.

This is overall good. Concept is okay. The “trap-laying” thing is the highlight and I think more creepiness can be put into that. Tone is okay but can be more objective, or cold-blooded.

item.title: The end?
item.content:encoded:
I really liked it at first, but the closer I got to the end, the less impressed I became. I felt like you just ran out of steam. And then there was that last bit about recovering the skip and that felt slapped on.

Downvote for me, unfortunately. It's definitely a fantastic idea, with a lot of potential, but that "ending" was just so jarring…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I believe this is qualifies as an SCP because it's not so explainable.

  1. This thing has heightened intelligence but is a colony of unicellular organisms, like a colony of bacteria, it shouldn't have aggregated intelligence but it does.
  2. This thing should be very easy to destroy, it's strength and resistance to being burned seems impossible.
  3. Finally, it should be kept as keter because if it's allowed to multiply imagine the consequences!!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Didn't like it much. It's basically just a generic "it catches you and kills you" monster without anything particularly scary or otherwise interesting about it, and I can't shake off the feeling that parts of the article are only here to ad shock value (how it slowly pulls victims appart, Members of Epsilon-9 being "at first" reluctant to use flamethrowers on their teammates. What relelvance does that anecdote even have in an acquisition report?).

Using a fake injured infant seems particularly overdone to me and I can't help but wonder how anyone falls for it seeing how according to the description it's made of tar, can barely move and can't make sounds; it seems it would be rather noticeable that something is amiss here.

item.title: Re: Why is it Keter?
item.content:encoded: The bit about it possibly learning to freeze parts of itself in order to use them as "bones" and become mobile definitely makes this not a Safe, but Keter seems too much. I'd say Euclid would be good here.

item.title: Why is it Keter?
item.content:encoded: It seems to be well contained, and even if it escapes, 60-80 kg of protein every 4 days means approximately 2-3 people / animals a week. If a nuclear bomb is deemed safe, Keter seems a bit much, no?
